items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: That was Mundell Lowe on 'Tumblebug'; did you know? Mundell couldn't read a note. He just had come out of Alabama.

ctx.x: It is still August 13 and we're continuing our discussion. I'm Bill Kirchner and we're talking with Eddie Sauter and we just started to talk about your writing for the Ray McKinley band, right after the war. I heard, Eddie, some of those things that you did. I went down to the Institute of Jazz Studies last week and played some of those 78's that you had recorded for Majestic, things like "Sandstorm", "Hangover Square", "Borderline" and "Tumblebug." What's your feeling about those pieces of music, were you…

Yes. That was part of my deal with Ray, that he should play these things, because I could never get Benny to do that. I would write what he needed, but he would also play what I would write, and he was pretty good about it. Sometimes he may not have wanted to and he did.
That was Mundell Lowe on 'Tumblebug'; did you know?
